parsed.rationale: Both `QualityTrend` and `ThermalDirection` are `type-alias-union` declarations in the same file (`Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/Wallpaper/Throttling/QualitySignal.swift`) within the `Wallpaper` package, and they share 3 fields structurally. However, their names encode distinct domain concepts — `QualityTrend` describes a direction of change in rendering/stream quality, while `ThermalDirection` describes a direction of change in device thermal state. The structural coincidence (both being small union type-aliases with the same arity) is almost certainly because both model a simple three-way directional signal (e.g., `up`/`down`/`stable`), not because they represent the same abstraction. Collapsing them into a single shared type would conflate two semantically independent domain signals and reduce clarity at call sites.
